guide.summary: Dropbox documents per-user OAuth 2.0 for user-scoped apps, and the App Folder option limits access to the /apps folder. Listing entries requires files.metadata.read through list_folder and list_folder/continue.

findings.title: Per-user OAuth token for the connected individual account
findings.detail: Apps that request only User API scopes receive a token associated with the user who authorizes the app. Authorization uses the OAuth code flow, with PKCE recommended for public clients.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects their own individual Dropbox account, with no team administration.

evidence.quote: Apps that request only scopes from the User API will receive a token associated with the user that authorizes the app.
Dropbox uses OAuth 2.0, an open specification, to authorize access to a user’s data. Once completed by a user, the OAuth flow returns an access token to your app. This

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — OAuth 2.0 token issued to a specific user. Use `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Public clients should use the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256).

findings.title: files.metadata.read scope for listing folder entries
findings.detail: The list_folder endpoint requires files.metadata.read and accepts App or User authentication. The response has has_more and cursor fields for continuation. This scope is the least privilege documented for these listing endpoints.
findings.appliesWhen: The app lists file and folder names in the app folder via list_folder.

evidence.quote: **Required scope:** `files.metadata.read` **Endpoint format:** RPC
**Authentication:** App, User, Dropbox-API-Select-Admin (Whole Team)
list_folder. **Required scope:** `files.metadata.read`

findings.title: Select App Folder content access in the Developer Console
findings.detail: App Folder access lets the app act only on data within its app folder, in the /apps folder. This option is suitable for apps that manage only their own content. The option limits the data boundary but does not make the scope read-only.
findings.appliesWhen: The app is created with App Folder content access to limit listing to the app folder.

findings.title: Register the app and configure redirect URIs before authorization
findings.detail: The app must be registered in the Developer Console to obtain an app key and secret, and exact redirect URIs must be registered under the OAuth 2 section of Settings. Redirect URI matching is checked at authorization time.
findings.appliesWhen: Before any customer authorization or token exchange is tested.

evidence.quote: Before you can get started, you'll need to register your app with Dropbox by creating a new app in the Developer Console. That page will guide you through the process
* You'll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the Developer Console for your application. Add them under **Redirect URIs** in the OAuth 2 section
of registering your app, selecting permissions, and obtaining an app key and secret (a.k.a. `client_id` and `client_secret`) and inputting redirect URIs.

findings.title: Generated tokens cover only the developer's own account
findings.detail: A token generated in the Developer Console is only for the developer's own account. Other customers must complete the standard OAuth flow, so testing with a generated token does not validate customer connections.

steps.title: Send the customer to Dropbox consent and verify the callback
steps.detail: Construct the authorization URL with client_id, redirect_uri and response_type=code, and send the customer to it. Dropbox redirects back to the registered URI with a code in the query string. Verify the callback arrived at the registered redirect URI before exchanging the code.
steps.doneWhen: The customer completes consent on dropbox.com and the callback URL contains a code parameter.

evidence.quote: 1. Construct a Dropbox authorization URL, with your application’s `client_id` and `redirect_uri` (if applicable) and specifying the `response_type` of `code`, and present it to the user

`https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=MY_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=MY_REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code` 2. Wait for the end user to complete authorization on dropbox.com, whom is then redirected back to your URI with an authorization code
* You'll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the Developer Console for your application. Add them under **Redirect URIs** in the OAuth 2 section

fields: code: query parameter returned on callback

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for a user access token and refresh token
steps.detail: Call the token endpoint with the code, client credentials and redirect_uri, using grant_type=authorization_code. Include token_access_type=offline on the authorization URL beforehand if background access is needed. Store the returned access token securely.
steps.doneWhen: The token response contains an access_token for the customer's account, and the token is stored server-side.

evidence.quote: 3. Call the /oauth2/token endpoint with your app’s `client_secret` to exchange the code for an access token in order to make API calls

When using refresh tokens, your call to the /oauth2/token endpoint with the `grant_type` of `authorization_code` will return a short-lived access token and a refresh token, which should be securely stored.

steps.title: List the first page of app folder entries
steps.detail: Call list_folder on the app folder root with the customer's access token. Set path to an empty string for the root of the app folder and recursive to false. The response includes entries, has_more and cursor. Return only names and types. Initial request paired with the continuation in continuations. Uses the same actionId and yields the cursor for continuation. First page of list_folder for the app folder root. Returns entries and cursor for continuation.
steps.doneWhen: The response returns entries with names and tags, plus has_more and cursor fields. Initial response returns a cursor and has_more value used by the continuation step. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: Successful response - `cursor` (string, required) — Pass the cursor into list_folder/continue to see what's changed in the folder since your previous query.
- `entries` (list of files.Metadata, required) — The files and (direct) subfolders in the folder.
- `has_more` (boolean, required) — If true, then there are more entries available. Pass the cursor to list_folder/continue to retrieve the rest.

fields: path: empty string means the app folder root

steps.title: Continue listing until has_more is false
steps.detail: Repeat list_folder/continue with the returned cursor while has_more is true. Stop when has_more is false; the listing is complete only then. Do not treat a single page as the full listing. Use the cursor from the prior page until has_more is false. Stop only when has_more is false.
steps.doneWhen: has_more is false on the final page; every page's entries are collected by name and type. has_more is false on the final page. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: - `cursor` (string, required) — The cursor returned by your last call to list_folder or list_folder/continue.
- `has_more` (boolean, required) — If true, then there are more entries available. Pass the cursor to list_folder/continue to retrieve the rest.
